docs.title: nowcastbdbv
docs.text:
The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BDBV) outbreak in the DRC as a case study: the hub's data streams, health zones and onset-to-report delays.

nowcastbdbv is the package in packages/nowcastbdbv of the repository (Packages).

docs.title: Install
docs.text: uv pip install "git+https://github.com/seabbs/bdbv-hub-modelling#subdirectory=packages/nowcastbdbv"

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
The hub publishes weekly confirmed cases by onset week, one block per release (vintage). tidy_target turns its files into a target table with the cases split into those with a known onset (observed) and an imputed one (imputed). load_target reads that table from data/ after uv run bdbvhub data. Here we make a small target table by hand for one province and two releases a week apart.

import pandas as pd

weeks = pd.date_range("2026-09-05", periods=4, freq="7D").date.astype(str)
rows = []
for vintage, totals in (
    ("2026-09-26", (6, 9, 12, 5)),
    ("2026-10-03", (6, 10, 15, 11)),
):
    for week, total in zip(weeks, totals):
        imputed = total // 3
        rows.append(
            (
                "real",
                vintage,
                vintage,
                "CD-NK",
                week,
                total - imputed,
                imputed,
                total,
            )
        )
target = pd.DataFrame(
    rows,
    columns=[
        "kind",
        "vintage",
        "cutoff",
        "location",
        "target_end_date",
        "observed",
        "imputed",
        "total",
    ],
)

vintages lists the releases in a table, and imputed_share gives the share of each week's cases with an imputed onset.

from nowcastbdbv.data.tidy import imputed_share, vintages

assert vintages(target) == ["2026-09-26", "2026-10-03"]
share = imputed_share(target)
assert share["imputed_share"].between(0, 1).all()

docs.title: See how recent weeks fill in
docs.text:
revision_table compares each release's counts with a later reference release. It is the reporting triangle in weekly form.

from nowcastbdbv.data.tidy import revision_table

revisions = revision_table(target)
first = revisions.loc[revisions["vintage"] == "2026-09-26"]
assert (first["fraction"] <= 1).all()

newly_missing gives the cases added between consecutive releases, split by onset status.

from nowcastbdbv.data.tidy import newly_missing

added = newly_missing(target)
assert added["new_total"].item() == 42 - 32
assert added["days"].item() == 7

docs.title: Key a hub release
docs.text:
The hub labels a release by its as_of date and may rewrite older labels a day later. release_id maps a label back to the one results and the submission ledger are keyed by.

from nowcastbdbv.data.tidy import release_id

assert release_id("2026-10-25") == "2026-10-24"
assert release_id("2026-11-01") == "2026-11-01"

docs.title: Estimate onset-to-report delays
docs.text:
empirical_pmf turns delays in days into a daily pmf, and delay_summary summarises them by group.

import numpy as np

from nowcastbdbv.data.delays import delay_summary, empirical_pmf

pmf = empirical_pmf([0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 40], max_delay=10)
assert np.isclose(pmf.sum(), 1.0)
delays = pd.DataFrame(
    {"vintage": "2026-10-03", "location": "CD-NK", "delay": [1, 2, 2, 4, 7]}
)
assert delay_summary(delays)["median"].item() == 2

hub_delay_pmf gives the pmf of the delay the hub uses to impute missing onsets at a release.

from nowcastbdbv.data.delays import hub_delay_pmf

hub = hub_delay_pmf("2026-10-24", max_delay=20)
assert np.isclose(hub.sum(), 1.0)

docs.title: Give places their populations and centres
docs.text:
Province populations and population-weighted centres ship with the package, as do the health zones' centres.

from nowcastbdbv.data.tidy import province_places
from nowcastbdbv.data.zones import PLACE_COLUMNS, zone_places

provinces = province_places(["CD-NK", "CD-IT"])
assert list(provinces.columns) == list(PLACE_COLUMNS)
zones = zone_places()
assert zones["location"].str.startswith("CD-NK-").any()

docs.title: nowcastbdbv.data.tidy
docs.text:
Download, tidy and load the BDBV Modeling Hub data.

The hub publishes these streams (see DATA_STREAMS):

  • target-data/time-series.csv: weekly confirmed cases by onset week, for the country, provinces and health zones, one block per as_of vintage. This is the target, observed plus imputed onsets.
  • auxiliary-data/daily-confirmed-case.csv: daily confirmed cases by onset day, split into observed and imputed onsets, per vintage.
  • auxiliary-data/weekly-reporting-delays-by-province.csv: one row per case with a known onset, giving its province, onset week and onset-to-report delay. Only the latest vintage is in the file. Earlier vintages are in archived-delay-data/ or only in the git history, so fetch_hub_data walks the history to find them all.
  • auxiliary-data/locations.csv and health-zone-code-mapping.csv: location codes, names and parents.
  • hub-config/: the round configuration, used for validation.

The hub publishes no deaths, suspected cases, report-date series or populations. Province populations come from a cited public source instead (PROVINCE_POPULATIONS).

A hub release is labelled by its as_of date. From the 2026-11-01 release on, as_of is the extraction date, one day after the last reported case. The hub states that earlier releases were labelled by the last reported case. release_id maps a label, as published or as the hub may rewrite it, to the label we key releases by, so results, the submission ledger and rounds keep their keys.

The tidy tables written by build_tidy_data are small and committed under data/. Raw downloads go to data/raw/ and are not committed.

def release_id(as_of: dt.date | str) -> str:
    """Return the label we key a hub release by.

    A label in `ORIGINAL_AS_OF` is kept. If the hub rewrites one a day
    later, it maps back. Other labels are kept.

    Parameters
    ----------
    as_of : datetime.date or str
        The release's `as_of`, as published or as rewritten.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The release's label, ISO formatted.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> release_id("2026-10-25"), release_id("2026-11-01")
    ('2026-10-24', '2026-11-01')
    """
    day = as_date(as_of)
    before = (day - dt.timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()
    return before if before in ORIGINAL_AS_OF else day.isoformat()

def load_province_centres() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load the population-weighted centres of all 26 provinces.

    The mean of health zone centroids weighted by WorldPop 2025 counts,
    with zone boundaries from the Ministry of Health shapefile on the
    Humanitarian Data Exchange, via INRB-UMIE/BDBV2026-Data
    (`build/drc_health_zones.geojson` at `f7d3907`, CC BY 4.0).
    This is the source and method of epiforecasts/BVDOutbreakSize. The
    file ships with the package, so it does not depend on the data
    directory.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `worldpop` and
        `zones`.
    """

    with path.open() as fh:
        return pd.read_csv(fh, comment="#")

def province_places(locations: Sequence[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return provinces' populations and centres, as task places.

    Parameters
    ----------
    locations : sequence of str

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame

        `latitude` and `longitude` (`PROVINCE_CENTRES`).
    """
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {

            "longitude": [PROVINCE_CENTRES[p][1] for p in locations],
        }
    )

def fetch_hub_data(
    raw_dir: Path | str,
    ref: str = "main",
    token: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Download the hub's data, including every vintage of the delay data.

    The latest versions of the files in `DATA_STREAMS` are taken from
    `ref`.
    For the delay data, every commit that touched `auxiliary-data/` is
    searched for delay files, and one file is kept per `as_of` vintage
    (from the most recent commit that has it).

    Parameters
    ----------
    raw_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        Where to save the files. Delay files go to `raw_dir/delays/`.
    ref : str
        Git ref of the hub to take the latest files from.
    token : str, optional
        GitHub token for the API. Defaults to `GITHUB_TOKEN` if set.
        Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 an hour, which is
        enough for one run.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A manifest with the commit SHA used and the source of each delay
        vintage. It is also written to `raw_dir/manifest.json`.
    """
    token = token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
    raw = Path(raw_dir)
    (raw / "delays").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    head = _api(f"repos/{HUB_REPO}/commits/{ref}", token)["sha"]
    for path in _LATEST_FILES:
        dest = raw / path
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest.write_bytes(_raw(head, path, token))

    commits = _api(
        f"repos/{HUB_REPO}/commits?path=auxiliary-data&sha={ref}&per_page=100",
        token,
    )
    delay_sources: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    for commit in commits:  # newest first
        sha = commit["sha"]
        tree = _api(f"repos/{HUB_REPO}/git/trees/{sha}?recursive=1", token)
        paths = [
            item["path"]
            for item in tree["tree"]
            if item["path"].startswith("auxiliary-data/")
            and "reporting-delays" in item["path"]
            and item["path"].endswith(".csv")
        ]
        for path in paths:
            content = _raw(sha, path, token)
            as_of = _delay_as_of(content, path)
            if as_of in delay_sources:
                continue
            (raw / "delays" / f"{as_of}.csv").write_bytes(content)
            delay_sources[as_of] = {"commit": sha, "path": path}
    manifest = {
        "repo": HUB_REPO,
        "ref": ref,
        "commit": head,
        "downloaded": dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "delay_vintages": dict(sorted(delay_sources.items())),
    }
    (raw / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")
    return manifest

def tidy_locations(locations_csv: Path | str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy the country and province rows of `locations.csv`.

    Adds the 2019 population (`PROVINCE_POPULATIONS`, summed for the
    country) and the province centre where known.

    Parameters
    ----------
    locations_csv : pathlib.Path or str
        Path to the hub's `auxiliary-data/locations.csv`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `location_name`, `location_type`,
        `population`, `latitude` and `longitude`.
    """
    loc = pd.read_csv(locations_csv)
    loc = loc.loc[loc["location_type"].isin(["country", "province"])].copy()
    pop = pd.Series(PROVINCE_POPULATIONS, dtype="int64")
    loc["population"] = loc["location"].map(pop)
    loc.loc[loc["location"] == "CD", "population"] = int(pop.sum())
    loc["population"] = loc["population"].astype("int64")
    loc["latitude"] = loc["location"].map(
        {k: v[0] for k, v in PROVINCE_CENTRES.items()}
    )
    loc["longitude"] = loc["location"].map(
        {k: v[1] for k, v in PROVINCE_CENTRES.items()}
    )
    cols = [
        "location",
        "location_name",
        "location_type",
        "population",
        "latitude",
        "longitude",
    ]
    return loc[cols].reset_index(drop=True)

def tidy_daily(daily_csv: Path | str, level: str = "province") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy daily onsets by vintage, for one level of geography.

    Parameters
    ----------
    daily_csv : pathlib.Path or str
        Path to the hub's `auxiliary-data/daily-confirmed-case.csv`.
    level : {"province", "zone"}
        The country and provinces, or the health zones, which are kept
        apart for a later zone stage.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `vintage`, `location`, `onset_date`, `observed` and
        `imputed`. Only days with at least one case are present.
    """
    types = {"province": ["country", "province"], "zone": ["health zone"]}
    if level not in types:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown level {level!r}: use {sorted(types)}.")
    raw = pd.read_csv(daily_csv)
    raw = raw.loc[raw["location_type"].isin(types[level])]
    raw = raw.assign(
        kind=np.where(raw["imputed"].astype(bool), "imputed", "observed")
    )
    wide = raw.pivot_table(
        index=["as_of", "location", "target_end_date"],
        columns="kind",
        values="observation",
        aggfunc="sum",
        fill_value=0,
    ).reset_index()
    for col in ("observed", "imputed"):
        if col not in wide.columns:
            wide[col] = 0
    wide = wide.rename(
        columns={"as_of": "vintage", "target_end_date": "onset_date"}
    )
    wide["vintage"] = wide["vintage"].map(release_id)
    wide.columns.name = None
    out = wide[["vintage", "location", "onset_date", "observed", "imputed"]]
    out = out.astype({"observed": "int64", "imputed": "int64"})
    return out.sort_values(["vintage", "location", "onset_date"]).reset_index(
        drop=True
    )

def tidy_target(
    time_series_csv: Path | str, daily: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy the target data for the country and provinces.

    Totals come from `time-series.csv`.
    The split into observed and imputed onsets comes from the daily file,
    summed into epi weeks.

    Parameters
    ----------
    time_series_csv : pathlib.Path or str
        Path to the hub's `target-data/time-series.csv`.
    daily : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `tidy_daily`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `kind` (always `"real"`), `vintage`, `location`,
        `location_name`, `target_end_date`, `observed`, `imputed` and
        `total`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If observed plus imputed does not equal the total in any row.
    """
    ts = pd.read_csv(time_series_csv)
    ts = ts.loc[
        (ts["target"] == TARGET)
        & ts["location_type"].isin(["country", "province"])
    ]
    ts = ts.rename(columns={"as_of": "vintage", "observation": "total"})
    ts["vintage"] = ts["vintage"].map(release_id)
    split = _weekly_split(daily)
    out = ts.merge(
        split, on=["vintage", "location", "target_end_date"], how="left"
    )
    out[["observed", "imputed"]] = (
        out[["observed", "imputed"]].fillna(0).astype("int64")
    )
    out["total"] = out["total"].astype("int64")
    bad = out["observed"] + out["imputed"] != out["total"]
    if bad.any():
        raise ValueError(
            f"{int(bad.sum())} rows where observed plus imputed is not "
            "the total."
        )
    out.insert(0, "kind", "real")
    cols = [
        "kind",
        "vintage",
        "location",
        "location_name",
        "target_end_date",
        "observed",
        "imputed",
        "total",
    ]
    return (
        out[cols]
        .sort_values(["vintage", "location", "target_end_date"])
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )

def tidy_delays(
    delay_files: Mapping[str, Path | str] | Path | str,
    locations: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy every vintage of the delay line data into one long table.

    Older files use a `location` column of short codes and newer files a
    `location_name` column, so both are mapped to hub location codes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    delay_files : mapping of str to path, or a directory
        Vintage to file, or a directory of `<vintage>.csv` files as
        written by `fetch_hub_data`.
    locations : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `tidy_locations`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per known-onset case, with columns `vintage`,
        `location`, `location_name`, `onset_week` (the Saturday ending
        the onset week) and `delay` (days from onset to report).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a province name cannot be mapped to a location code.
    """
    if isinstance(delay_files, Path | str):
        files = {p.stem: p for p in sorted(Path(delay_files).glob("*.csv"))}
    else:
        files = {k: Path(v) for k, v in delay_files.items()}
    codes = _province_code_map(locations)
    names = dict(
        zip(locations["location"], locations["location_name"], strict=True)
    )
    frames = []
    for vintage, path in sorted(files.items()):
        df = pd.read_csv(path)
        key = "location_name" if "location_name" in df.columns else "location"
        loc = df[key].map(codes)
        if loc.isna().any():
            missing = sorted(set(df.loc[loc.isna(), key]))
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown provinces in {path}: {missing}")
        frames.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "vintage": release_id(vintage),
                    "location": loc,
                    "location_name": loc.map(names),
                    "onset_week": df["week_ending"].astype(str),
                    "delay": df["days_sym_to_report"].astype("int64"),
                }
            )
        )
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    return out.sort_values(
        ["vintage", "location", "onset_week", "delay"]
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

def build_tidy_data(
    raw_dir: Path | str, out_dir: Path | str
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Tidy the raw downloads and write the tables to `out_dir`.

    Writes `locations.csv`, `target.csv`, `daily.csv`,
    `daily_zones.csv.gz`, `delays.csv.gz`, `health_zones.csv.gz` and
    `national-coherence.csv` (see `national_coherence`), and copies the
    hub configuration to `hub-config/` and the download manifest to
    `sources.json`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    raw_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        Directory written by `fetch_hub_data`.
    out_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        Directory for the tidy tables, usually `data/`.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to pandas.DataFrame
        The tidy tables, keyed by name.
    """
    raw, out = Path(raw_dir), Path(out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    locations = tidy_locations(raw / "auxiliary-data" / "locations.csv")
    daily_csv = raw / "auxiliary-data" / "daily-confirmed-case.csv"
    daily = tidy_daily(daily_csv)
    delays = tidy_delays(raw / "delays", locations)
    # Every table keyed by release carries the release's latest onset day.
    cutoffs = latest_onset_days(daily)
    series = raw / "target-data" / "time-series.csv"
    by_release = {
        "target": tidy_target(series, daily),
        "daily": daily,
        "daily_zones": tidy_daily(daily_csv, level="zone"),
        "delays": delays,
        "health_zones": tidy_health_zones(series),
    }
    tables = {"locations": locations} | {
        name: table.assign(cutoff=table["vintage"].map(cutoffs))
        for name, table in by_release.items()
    }
    files = {
        "locations": "locations.csv",
        "target": "target.csv",
        "daily": "daily.csv",
        "daily_zones": "daily_zones.csv.gz",
        "delays": "delays.csv.gz",
        "health_zones": "health_zones.csv.gz",
    }
    for name, file in files.items():
        write_csv(tables[name], out / file)
    write_csv(
        national_coherence(tables["target"]),
        out / "national-coherence.csv",
    )
    config = out / "hub-config"
    config.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for path in (raw / "hub-config").glob("*.json"):
        (config / path.name).write_text(path.read_text())
    manifest = raw / "manifest.json"
    if manifest.exists():
        (out / "sources.json").write_text(manifest.read_text())
    return tables

def national_coherence(
    target: pd.DataFrame, national: str = "CD"
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compare the national counts with the sum of the provinces.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Tidy target table (`tidy_target` or `load_target`).
    national : str
        Location code of the country.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per kind, vintage, onset week and stream (`observed`,
        `imputed`, `total`), with the national count, the sum of the
        provinces and `gap` (national minus provinces). A week missing on
        one side counts as zero there.
    """
    keys = ["kind", "vintage", "target_end_date"]
    streams = list(COHERENCE_STREAMS)
    nat = (
        target.loc[target["location"] == national].groupby(keys)[streams].sum()
    )
    prov = (
        target.loc[target["location"] != national].groupby(keys)[streams].sum()
    )
    nat, prov = nat.align(prov, join="outer", fill_value=0)
    long = nat.reset_index().melt(
        id_vars=keys, var_name="stream", value_name="national"
    )
    long["provinces"] = (
        prov.reset_index()
        .melt(id_vars=keys, var_name="stream", value_name="provinces")[
            "provinces"
        ]
        .to_numpy()
    )
    long["gap"] = long["national"] - long["provinces"]
    return long.sort_values([*keys, "stream"]).reset_index(drop=True)

def zone_coherence(
    target: pd.DataFrame, zones: pd.DataFrame, national: str = "CD"
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compare each province and the country with the sum of their zones.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Tidy target table (`load_target`); its real rows are used.
    zones : pandas.DataFrame
        The hub's weekly health zone counts (`load_health_zones`), with
        `vintage`, `location`, `province`, `target_end_date` and `total`.
    national : str
        Location code of the country.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per vintage, week and parent: `level` (`province` or
        `national`), `location` (the parent), `parent` (its total),
        `zones` (the sum of its zones) and `gap` (parent minus zones),
        cases in no zone where positive. A week missing on one side counts
        as zero there, so a province with no zone rows shows its whole
        count as a gap.
    """
    keys = ["vintage", "target_end_date"]
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    prov = real.loc[real["location"].str.count("-") == 1]
    parent = prov.groupby([*keys, "location"])["total"].sum()
    from_zones = (
        zones.rename(columns={"location": "zone"})
        .groupby([*keys, "province"])["total"]
        .sum()
    )
    from_zones.index = from_zones.index.set_names([*keys, "location"])
    parent, from_zones = parent.align(from_zones, join="outer", fill_value=0)
    provinces = (
        pd.DataFrame({"parent": parent, "zones": from_zones})
        .reset_index()
        .assign(level="province")
    )
    nat = real.loc[real["location"] == national].groupby(keys)["total"].sum()
    all_zones = zones.groupby(keys)["total"].sum()
    nat, all_zones = nat.align(all_zones, join="outer", fill_value=0)
    country = (
        pd.DataFrame({"parent": nat, "zones": all_zones})
        .reset_index()
        .assign(level="national", location=national)
    )
    out = pd.concat([provinces, country], ignore_index=True)
    out["gap"] = out["parent"] - out["zones"]
    cols = [*keys, "level", "location", "parent", "zones", "gap"]
    return out[cols].sort_values(cols[:4]).reset_index(drop=True)

def delays_for_vintage(
    delays: pd.DataFrame, vintage: str
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, str]:
    """Delay rows for a vintage, using the latest earlier one if it has none.

    The hub does not publish delays with every vintage (2026-08-18 has
    none) and can publish them late. Rather than fail, the latest delay
    vintage on or before `vintage` stands in, relabelled to `vintage`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    delays : pandas.DataFrame
        Tidy delay rows with a `vintage` column.
    vintage : str
        The data vintage being forecast from.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of pandas.DataFrame and str
        The delay table with rows for `vintage`, and a note of what was
        used instead (empty when the vintage had its own delays).
    """
    if delays.empty or (delays["vintage"] == vintage).any():
        return delays, ""
    earlier = sorted(str(v) for v in delays["vintage"].unique() if v <= vintage)
    if not earlier:
        return delays, (
            f"delays: none published by {vintage}, so the model's default "
            "completeness lag was used"
        )
    use = earlier[-1]
    extra = delays.loc[delays["vintage"] == use].assign(vintage=vintage)
    note = (
        f"delays: none published for {vintage}, so used the {use} delays, "
        "the latest available"
    )
    return pd.concat([delays, extra], ignore_index=True), note

def coherence_summary(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    vintage: str,
    national: str = "CD",
    zones: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Summarise national coherence for one real vintage.

    This is the `coherence.json` record the submission CI reads (see
    `packages/bdbvsubmission/INTEGRATION.md`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Tidy target table.
    vintage : str
        The real vintage to check.
    national : str
        Location code of the country.
    zones : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        The hub's weekly health zone counts. With them, `zones` summarises
        each province and the country against their zones
        (`zone_coherence`).

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `as_of`, `coherent`, per-stream summaries, the rows with a gap,
        how the models handle a gap and, with `zones`, the zones' summary:
        `coherent`, the province and national weeks with a gap,
        `unassigned_cases` (the country's cases in no zone),
        `unassigned_share` and the rows with a gap.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the vintage has no real data.
    """
    rows = target.loc[
        (target["kind"] == "real") & (target["vintage"] == vintage)
    ]
    if rows.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"No real data for vintage {vintage}.")
    table = national_coherence(rows, national)
    gaps = table.loc[table["gap"] != 0]
    streams = {
        s: {
            "weeks_with_gap": int((g["gap"] != 0).sum()),
            "max_abs_gap": int(g["gap"].abs().max()) if len(g) else 0,
            "total_gap": int(g["gap"].sum()),
        }
        for s, g in table.groupby("stream")
    }
    return {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "as_of": vintage,
        "national": national,
        "coherent": gaps.empty,
        "streams": streams,
        "rows": [
            {
                "target_end_date": str(r["target_end_date"]),
                "stream": str(r["stream"]),
                "national": int(r["national"]),
                "provinces": int(r["provinces"]),
                "gap": int(r["gap"]),
            }
            for r in gaps.to_dict("records")
        ],
        "handling": COHERENCE_HANDLING,
        **(
            {}
            if zones is None
            else {"zones": _zone_summary(target, zones, vintage, national)}
        ),
    }

def newly_missing(target: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return cases added between consecutive vintages, by onset status.

    For each location and each vintage after the first, the change in
    total observed and total imputed onsets since the previous vintage of
    the same kind.
    The imputed change approximates the number of cases without an onset
    reported between the two vintages.
    It is net of cases whose onset was filled in later, so it can be
    negative.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        A target table.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `kind`, `location`, `vintage`, `previous_vintage`,
        `days` (between the two releases' cut-offs), `new_observed`,
        `new_imputed`, `new_total` and `new_imputed_share`.
    """
    sums = target.groupby(
        ["kind", "location", "vintage", "cutoff"], as_index=False
    )[["observed", "imputed", "total"]].sum()
    sums = sums.sort_values(["kind", "location", "vintage"])
    grp = sums.groupby(["kind", "location"])
    sums["previous_vintage"] = grp["vintage"].shift(1)
    sums["previous_cutoff"] = grp["cutoff"].shift(1)
    for col in ("observed", "imputed", "total"):
        sums[f"new_{col}"] = sums[col] - grp[col].shift(1)
    out = sums.dropna(subset=["previous_vintage"]).copy()
    out["days"] = (
        pd.to_datetime(out["cutoff"]) - pd.to_datetime(out["previous_cutoff"])
    ).dt.days
    new_total = out["new_total"].where(out["new_total"] > 0)
    out["new_imputed_share"] = out["new_imputed"] / new_total
    cols = [
        "kind",
        "location",
        "vintage",
        "previous_vintage",
        "days",
        "new_observed",
        "new_imputed",
        "new_total",
        "new_imputed_share",
    ]
    out = out[cols].astype(
        {"new_observed": "int64", "new_imputed": "int64", "new_total": "int64"}
    )
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

def revision_table(
    target: pd.DataFrame, reference_vintage: str | None = None
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compare each vintage's counts with a later reference vintage.

    This is the reporting triangle in weekly form: how recent weeks fill
    in as later vintages arrive.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        A target table of one kind.
    reference_vintage : str, optional
        The vintage to compare against. Defaults to the latest.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `vintage`, `cutoff`, `location`, `target_end_date`,
        `weeks_before` (whole weeks from the target week to the epi week
        of the vintage's cut-off),
        `total`, `reference_total` and `fraction` (`total` over
        `reference_total`, missing where the latter is zero).
    """
    ref = reference_vintage or max(target["vintage"])
    latest = target.loc[
        target["vintage"] == ref, ["location", "target_end_date", "total"]
    ].rename(columns={"total": "reference_total"})
    out = target.loc[
        target["vintage"] <= ref,
        ["vintage", "cutoff", "location", "target_end_date", "total"],
    ].merge(latest, on=["location", "target_end_date"], how="left")
    out["reference_total"] = out["reference_total"].fillna(0)
    out["weeks_before"] = _weeks_before(out["cutoff"], out["target_end_date"])
    out["fraction"] = out["total"] / out["reference_total"].where(
        out["reference_total"] > 0
    )
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

def cutoff_window(
    daily: pd.DataFrame, vintage: str, location: str, weeks: int = 4
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return one release's daily onsets for the weeks up to its cut-off.

    This shows how the hub's weekly target forms from daily onsets,
    including the partial week that holds the cut-off.

    Parameters
    ----------
    daily : pandas.DataFrame
        Daily onsets, as from `load_daily`.
    vintage : str
        The release.
    location : str
        The place.
    weeks : int
        Epi weeks to keep, ending with the cut-off's week.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per day from the first kept week's Sunday to the
        cut-off, with days without onsets filled with zero. Columns
        `onset_date`, `target_end_date`, `observed`, `imputed`, `total`,
        `week_days` (days of the week up to the cut-off), `partial`
        (fewer than seven) and `week_total` (the week's total).
    """
    rows = daily.loc[
        (daily["vintage"] == vintage) & (daily["location"] == location)
    ]
    cutoff = pd.Timestamp(rows["cutoff"].iloc[0])
    end = pd.Timestamp(epiweek_end(cutoff.date()))
    days = pd.date_range(end - pd.Timedelta(days=7 * weeks - 1), cutoff)
    out = (
        rows.assign(onset_date=pd.to_datetime(rows["onset_date"]))
        .set_index("onset_date")[["observed", "imputed"]]
        .reindex(days, fill_value=0)
        .rename_axis("onset_date")
        .reset_index()
    )
    out["total"] = out["observed"] + out["imputed"]
    out["target_end_date"] = [
        epiweek_end(d.date()).isoformat() for d in out["onset_date"]
    ]
    out["onset_date"] = out["onset_date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    week = out.groupby("target_end_date")
    out["week_days"] = week["total"].transform("size")
    out["partial"] = out["week_days"] < 7
    out["week_total"] = week["total"].transform("sum")
    return out[
        [
            "onset_date",
            "target_end_date",
            "observed",
            "imputed",
            "total",
            "week_days",
            "partial",
            "week_total",
        ]
    ]

def release_updates(counts: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return how each week's count changed between consecutive releases.

    Parameters
    ----------
    counts : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `vintage`, `cutoff`, `location`, `target_end_date` and
        `total`. A place and week missing from a release has no cases in
        it, as in the health zone table.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per release after the first, place and week of the earlier
        release that has cases in either, with `vintage` (the later
        release), `previous`, `location`, `target_end_date`,
        `weeks_before` (whole weeks from the week to the epi week of the
        earlier release's cut-off), `previous_total`, `total` and `change`.
    """
    keys = ["location", "target_end_date"]
    releases = sorted(counts["vintage"].unique())
    cutoffs = counts.groupby("vintage")["cutoff"].first()
    frames: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    for prev, vin in pairwise(releases):
        old = counts.loc[counts["vintage"] == prev, [*keys, "total"]]
        new = counts.loc[
            (counts["vintage"] == vin)
            & counts["target_end_date"].between(
                old["target_end_date"].min(), old["target_end_date"].max()
            ),
            [*keys, "total"],
        ]
        pair = old.merge(
            new, on=keys, how="outer", suffixes=("_previous", "")
        ).fillna({"total_previous": 0, "total": 0})
        pair = pair.loc[(pair["total_previous"] > 0) | (pair["total"] > 0)]
        frames.append(
            pair.rename(columns={"total_previous": "previous_total"}).assign(
                vintage=vin, previous=prev
            )
        )
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    out[["previous_total", "total"]] = out[["previous_total", "total"]].astype(
        "int64"
    )
    out["change"] = out["total"] - out["previous_total"]
    out["weeks_before"] = _weeks_before(
        out["previous"].map(cutoffs), out["target_end_date"]
    )
    cols = [
        "vintage",
        "previous",
        *keys,
        "weeks_before",
        "previous_total",
        "total",
        "change",
    ]
    return out[cols]

def downward_summary(updates: pd.DataFrame, by: Sequence[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Summarise how often and how much counts fell between releases.

    Parameters
    ----------
    updates : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `release_updates`.
    by : sequence of str
        Columns to summarise within, such as `("location",)`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The `by` columns with `weeks` (place-weeks compared), `fell`,
        `share_fell`, `cases_down` and `cases_up` (summed falls and rises),
        `downward_share` (`cases_down` over the summed absolute change)
        and `largest_fall`.
    """
    down = (-updates["change"]).clip(lower=0)
    up = updates["change"].clip(lower=0)
    frame = updates.assign(
        fell=updates["change"] < 0, cases_down=down, cases_up=up
    )
    out = frame.groupby(list(by)).agg(
        weeks=("change", "size"),
        fell=("fell", "sum"),
        cases_down=("cases_down", "sum"),
        cases_up=("cases_up", "sum"),
        largest_fall=("cases_down", "max"),
    )
    out["share_fell"] = out["fell"] / out["weeks"]
    moved = out["cases_down"] + out["cases_up"]
    out["downward_share"] = out["cases_down"] / moved.where(moved > 0)
    cols = [
        "weeks",
        "fell",
        "share_fell",
        "cases_down",
        "cases_up",
        "downward_share",
        "largest_fall",
    ]
    return out[cols].reset_index()

docs.text:
Onset-to-report delay distributions.

The interface is small. A DelayModel is fitted to the delay line data of one vintage and returns a DelayFit. A DelayFit gives a daily pmf for any province and onset week, so a model can use delays that vary by place and time.

EmpiricalDelayModel takes the empirical pmf over a rolling window of onset weeks and shrinks each province towards the pooled pmf, so small provinces and recent weeks stay stable. It ignores right truncation and the weekly censoring of onset, so recent delays are biased short.

The renewal models fit their own delay with the cases, as the Delays section of the Renewal models methods page describes. hub_delay_pmf gives the delay the hub draws from to impute missing onsets, in closed form.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EmpiricalDelayFit:
    """Empirical delay pmfs by province and onset week.

    Attributes
    ----------
    pooled : numpy.ndarray
        The pmf over all provinces and weeks.
    by_cell : dict
        `(location, onset_week)` to pmf.
    max_delay : int
        Longest delay.
    """

    pooled: NDArray[np.float64]
    by_cell: dict[tuple[str, str], NDArray[np.float64]] = field(
        default_factory=dict
    )
    max_delay: int = DEFAULT_MAX_DELAY

    def pmf(self, location: str, onset_week: str) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
        """Return the pmf for a cell, or the pooled pmf if it is not known.

        Parameters
        ----------
        location : str
            Province code.
        onset_week : str
            The Saturday ending the onset week.

        Returns
        -------
        numpy.ndarray
            Probabilities for delays 0 to `max_delay`.
        """
        return self.by_cell.get((location, onset_week), self.pooled)

    def cdf(self, location: str, onset_week: str) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
        """Return the cumulative probabilities for a cell.

        Parameters
        ----------
        location : str
            Province code.
        onset_week : str
            The Saturday ending the onset week.

        Returns
        -------
        numpy.ndarray
            `P(delay <= d)` for d from 0 to `max_delay`.
        """
        return np.cumsum(self.pmf(location, onset_week))

    def quantile(self, q: float) -> int:
        """Return a quantile of the pooled delay, in whole days.

        Parameters
        ----------
        q : float
            Probability in (0, 1].

        Returns
        -------
        int
            The smallest delay whose pooled cdf reaches `q`.
        """
        return int(np.searchsorted(np.cumsum(self.pooled), q))

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EmpiricalDelayModel:
    r"""Rolling-window empirical delays with shrinkage to the pooled pmf.

    For province $p$ and onset week $w$, with $n_{pw}$ delays in the
    window and their empirical pmf $\hat f_{pw}$, the estimate is

    $$
    \tilde f_{pw} = \frac{n_{pw} \hat f_{pw} + k \hat f_{w}}{n_{pw} + k},
    $$

    where $\hat f_w$ is the pmf pooled over provinces in the same window
    and $k$ is `prior_weight`.
    This is the posterior mean under a Dirichlet prior centred on the
    pooled pmf.
    With no change over time or place it reduces to the pooled pmf.

    Attributes
    ----------
    window_weeks : int
        Width of the rolling window of onset weeks, centred where
        possible. Use a large number for a static delay.
    prior_weight : float
        Pseudo-count $k$ pulling each province to the pooled pmf.
    max_delay : int
        Longest delay kept.
    """

    window_weeks: int = 5
    prior_weight: float = 50.0
    max_delay: int = DEFAULT_MAX_DELAY

    def fit(self, delays: pd.DataFrame, vintage: str) -> EmpiricalDelayFit:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Fit to the delay line data of one vintage.

        Parameters
        ----------
        delays : pandas.DataFrame
            Delay line data with `location`, `onset_week` and `delay`.
        vintage : str
            Not used: this estimator ignores right truncation.

        Returns
        -------
        EmpiricalDelayFit
            Pooled and per-cell pmfs.
        """
        pooled = empirical_pmf(delays["delay"], self.max_delay)
        weeks = sorted(set(delays["onset_week"].astype(str)))
        half = self.window_weeks // 2
        by_cell: dict[tuple[str, str], NDArray[np.float64]] = {}
        week_idx = {w: i for i, w in enumerate(weeks)}
        idx = delays["onset_week"].astype(str).map(week_idx).to_numpy()
        for i, week in enumerate(weeks):
            in_window = np.abs(idx - i) <= half
            window = delays.loc[in_window]
            pooled_w = empirical_pmf(window["delay"], self.max_delay)
            n_w = int(pooled_w.sum() > 0)
            centre = pooled_w if n_w else pooled
            for loc, rows in window.groupby("location"):
                counts = empirical_pmf(rows["delay"], self.max_delay)
                n = float(
                    (
                        (rows["delay"] >= 0) & (rows["delay"] <= self.max_delay)
                    ).sum()
                )
                by_cell[(str(loc), week)] = (
                    n * counts + self.prior_weight * centre
                ) / (n + self.prior_weight)
        return EmpiricalDelayFit(pooled, by_cell, self.max_delay)

def empirical_pmf(
    delays: Sequence[int] | NDArray[np.int64] | pd.Series,
    max_delay: int = DEFAULT_MAX_DELAY,
) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
    """Return the empirical daily pmf of a set of delays.

    Negative delays and delays above `max_delay` are dropped.

    Parameters
    ----------
    delays : array-like of int
        Delays in days.
    max_delay : int
        Longest delay kept.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Probabilities for delays 0 to `max_delay`. All zero if no delays
        are left.
    """
    d = np.asarray(delays, dtype=np.int64)
    d = d[(d >= 0) & (d <= max_delay)]
    counts = np.bincount(d, minlength=max_delay + 1).astype(np.float64)
    total = counts.sum()
    return counts / total if total > 0 else counts

def hub_delay_pmf(
    release: dt.date | str,
    max_delay: int = DEFAULT_MAX_DELAY,
) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
    r"""Return the daily pmf of the hub's imputed onset delay at a release.

    The hub puts the onset of a case without one at report hour
    $U \sim \mathrm{Unif}(0, 24)$ minus a delay $X$ in hours drawn from a
    generalised gamma (`auxiliary-data/imputation-details.md`), so the
    onset is $k = \lceil (X - U) / 24 \rceil$ days before the report.
    That is the double interval censored pmf of $X / 24$ days,
    primarycensored's `dpcens(k, pgengamma, pwindow = 1, swindow = 1)`,
    in closed form from `nowcastrenewal.components.pmfs`.
    The generalised gamma is fitted to the delays published at 2026-10-17
    as exact before `HUB_DOUBLE_CENSORED_FROM` and as double interval
    censored from then on, with the parameters in
    `HUB_GENGAMMA`. Truncated at `max_delay` and renormalised.

    Parameters
    ----------
    release : datetime.date or str
        The release date.
    max_delay : int
        Longest delay kept.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        $\hat f$ on days 0 to `max_delay`.
    """
    # The model package needs PyRenew, which the data layer does not.
    from nowcastrenewal.components.pmfs import Delay, delay_pmf

    fit = (
        "double_censored"
        if as_date(release) >= HUB_DOUBLE_CENSORED_FROM
        else "exact"
    )
    mu, sigma, q = HUB_GENGAMMA[fit]
    return delay_pmf(Delay("gengamma", mu - np.log(24), sigma, q), max_delay)

    config = json.loads(Path(tasks_json).read_text())

    geo = json.loads(download(_raw(BVD_REPO, bvd_tag, BOUNDARIES_PATH)))

    ]

        `data.zones.hub_places()` from the default data directory.

    Returns
    -------
    list of ForecastTask
        Tasks ordered by kind and vintage.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import dataclasses
    >>> from nowcastbdbv.data.tidy import (
    ...     delays_for_vintage, load_daily, load_delays, load_target
    ... )
    >>> from nowcasteval import backtest as bt
    >>> target = load_target()
    >>> real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    >>> config = dataclasses.replace(
    ...     bt.load_config("packages/nowcastbdbv/config/backtest.toml"),
    ...     min_horizon=-6,
    ... )
    >>> vintage = "2026-10-17"
    >>> task = bt.make_tasks(
    ...     real.loc[real["vintage"] == vintage],
    ...     delays_for_vintage(load_delays(), vintage)[0],
    ...     config,
    ...     history=real,
    ...     daily=load_daily(),
    ... )[0]
    >>> task.reference_date, task.target_end_dates[-1]
    """
    tasks = []
    source = target if history is None else history
    if places is None:
        places = hub_places()
    imputation = functools.cache(_imputation_delay)
    for (kind, vintage), rows in target.groupby(["kind", "vintage"]):
        mine = source["kind"] == kind
        past_target = source.loc[mine & (source["vintage"] <= vintage)]
        ref = reference_date_for_vintage(str(vintage))
        dly, history = None, None
        if delays is not None:
            mask = delays["vintage"] == vintage
            if "kind" in delays.columns:
                mask &= delays["kind"] == kind
            sel = delays.loc[mask]
            dly = sel if not sel.empty else None
            same = delays["vintage"] <= vintage
            if "kind" in delays.columns:
                same &= delays["kind"] == kind
            past = delays.loc[same]
            history = past if not past.empty else None
        task = ForecastTask(
            vintage=str(vintage),
            reference_date=ref,
            kind=str(kind),
            cutoff=release_cutoff(rows, str(vintage)).isoformat(),
            target=rows.reset_index(drop=True),
            delays=dly,
            delay_history=history,
            target_history=past_target if not past_target.empty else None,
            daily_history=_daily_for(daily, str(kind), str(vintage)),
            **_zone_fields(zones, str(kind), str(vintage)),
            imputation_delay=imputation(str(vintage)),
            places=places,
            locations=forecast_locations(rows),
            target_end_dates=forecast_weeks(ref, config),
            n_samples=config.n_samples,
            seed=config.seed,
            max_delay=config.max_delay,
            report_by={
                d: release_cutoff(source.loc[mine], d).isoformat()
                for d in sorted(report_by)
                if kind != "simulated" and d > str(vintage)
            },
        )
        # A cumulative first release is not part of the reporting.
        tasks.append(without_cumulative_first_release(task))
    return tasks

    daily: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    extra_weeks: int = 0,
    *,
    zones: ZoneData | None = None,
    places: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
) -> tuple[ForecastTask, str]:
    """Build the task of one real vintage, as the submission fits it.

    The fit store fits the same task (`bdbvhub.store.store.origin_tasks`),
    so the submission and the store give a fit the same key. The weeks run from
    `TASK_MIN_HORIZON`. A vintage with no delays of its own uses the
    latest earlier ones (`delays_for_vintage`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    target, delays : pandas.DataFrame
        The tidy target and delay tables.
    config : BacktestConfig
        Horizons, samples and seed (`[forecast]`).
    vintage : str
        A real vintage.
    daily : pandas.DataFrame, optional

        one, so its fit also covers the next round's weeks.
    zones : ZoneData, optional

    places : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        The task's places (`make_tasks`).

        config,
        min_horizon=TASK_MIN_HORIZON,
        max_horizon=config.max_horizon + extra_weeks,

    rows = real.loc[real["vintage"] == vintage]

    task = make_tasks(
        rows,
        used,
        config,
        history=real,
        daily=daily,
        zones=zones,
        places=places,
    )[0]
    return task, note

def run_lopo(
    models: Sequence[ForecastModel],
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    delays: pd.DataFrame,
    config: BacktestConfig,
    *,
    provinces: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    fits: list[pd.DataFrame] | None = None,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Leave one province out: forecast it with its counts masked.

    For each development task and each province with cases, the model
    gets the task with that province in `ForecastTask.mask`
    (`lopo_tasks`).
    Only the masked province's forecast is kept and scored, against the
    latest real vintage.
    Models without `supports_mask = True` cannot honour a mask and are
    skipped.

    Parameters
    ----------
    models : sequence of ForecastModel
        Models to check.
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        The tidy target table.
    delays : pandas.DataFrame
        The tidy delay table.
    config : BacktestConfig
        Settings.
    provinces : sequence of str, optional
        Provinces to mask, one at a time. Defaults to every province with
        cases in each task.
    fits : list, optional
        Collects fit summaries, as for `run_forecasts`.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of pandas.DataFrame
        The forecasts, with a `masked` column, and the scores. Both empty
        if no model supports a mask.
    """
    able = [m for m in models if getattr(m, "supports_mask", False)]
    for m in models:
        if m not in able:
            log.info("Skipping %s in leave-one-province-out: no mask.", m.name)
    if not able:
        return pd.DataFrame(), pd.DataFrame()
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    latest = real_vintages(real)[-1]
    frames = []
    for task in lopo_tasks(target, delays, config, provinces=provinces):
        prov = task.mask[0]
        samples = run_forecasts(able, [task], fits)
        kept = samples.loc[samples["location"] == prov].copy()
        kept.insert(4, "masked", prov)
        frames.append(kept)
    forecasts = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    scores = score_tasks(
        forecasts,
        truth_from_vintage(real, latest),
        latest,
        config.complete_after_weeks,
    )
    return forecasts, scores

Zone backtest: the random walks' zone runs, scored on later releases.

The fit store holds each walk's run on every hub zone at each origin, made on each zone's own release snapshots (bdbvhub.store.store.walk_zones). score_zones scores them at every real vintage before the truth vintage, for every zone with cases at the vintage (bdbvhub.store.store.stored_zone_forecasts); the CLI's zone-backtest reads them from the store. The zone delay, observation model and walk spread are each the zone's own where it has at least 10 cases a week, else its province's, else national (pooling). Each model is scored on its zone samples as stored, the form submitted. Zones are scored on the zone count each later real vintage reports. randomwalk is scored on its samples as they are, with no delay. randomwalknowcast's final-count samples are drawn as for provinces (nowcasteval.nowcast.draw_reported) under its own zone delay at the origin. The energy score takes every zone and week of an origin and release as one vector, from the same drawn samples.

def score_zones(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    delays: pd.DataFrame | None,
    daily: pd.DataFrame,
    daily_zones: pd.DataFrame,
    run: ZoneForecasts,
    config: BacktestConfig | None = None,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Score zone forecasts on later releases.

    Two targets are scored, as for the provinces (`release_backtest`): what
    each later release reported, and the complete weeks of the latest
    release, decided by `complete_weeks` from the zone counts of every
    release, a week with no onset counting as 0.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        The province target table (`load_target`).
    delays : pandas.DataFrame or None
        The delay table (`load_delays`).
    daily : pandas.DataFrame
        The daily table of the country and provinces (`load_daily`).
    daily_zones : pandas.DataFrame
        The daily zone table (`load_daily_zones`).
    run : ZoneForecasts
        The forecasts, such as the walks' stored zone runs. Every
        release is still read for the truth and the complete weeks.
    config : BacktestConfig, optional
        The seed of the reported-count draws. Defaults to
        `BacktestConfig()`.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of pandas.DataFrame
        The scores, `score_forecasts` output with `model`, `origin`,
        `target` (`"reported"` or `"complete"`), `truth_vintage` and
        `horizon` in weeks
        from the reference date, one row per model, origin, later
        vintage, zone and week.
        Then `energy_scores` of every model's zones by `origin`, `target`
        and `truth_vintage`, from the same drawn samples. Then the zone
        forecasts, as submitted, under each model's name: `model`,
        `origin`, `reference_date`, `location`, `target_end_date`,
        `sample` and `value`.
    """
    config = config or BacktestConfig()
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    vintages = real_vintages(real)
    latest = vintages[-1]
    done = _complete_zone_weeks(daily_zones, daily, vintages)
    latest_counts = weekly_counts(daily_zones, latest)
    runs = run.runs.astype({"origin": str})
    frames, energy, kept = [], [], []
    for vintage in vintages[:-1]:
        here = runs.loc[runs["origin"] == vintage, "model"].astype(str)
        if here.empty:
            continue
        task = _zone_task(real, delays, daily, config, vintage)
        counts = weekly_counts(daily_zones, vintage)
        forecasts: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
        summaries: dict[str, pd.DataFrame | None] = {}
        for name in here:
            mine = (run.samples["key"] == name) & (
                run.samples["origin"].astype(str) == vintage
            )
            forecasts[name] = (
                run.samples.loc[mine]
                .drop(columns=["key", "origin"])
                .reset_index(drop=True)
            )
            summaries[name] = model_origin_rows(run.delays, name, vintage)
            kept.append(
                forecasts[name].assign(
                    model=name,
                    origin=vintage,
                    reference_date=task.reference_date.isoformat(),
                )
            )
        if not forecasts:
            continue
        reported = counts.rename(columns={"total": "reported"})[
            ["location", "target_end_date", "reported"]
        ]
        # Each model draws from its own stream, as in release_backtest.
        rngs = {name: task.rng(name) for name in forecasts}
        later = [v for v in vintages if v > vintage]
        by_model = {
            key: reported_samples(
                samples,
                summaries[key],
                key,
                vintage,
                later,
                daily,
                reported,
                rngs[key],
            )
            for key, samples in forecasts.items()
        }
        for o2 in later:
            drawn = [
                draws[o2].assign(
                    model=key,
                    origin=vintage,
                    target="reported",
                    truth_vintage=o2,
                )
                for key, draws in by_model.items()
                if o2 in draws
            ]
            if not drawn:
                continue
            both = pd.concat(drawn, ignore_index=True)
            truth = _zone_truth(weekly_counts(daily_zones, o2), both, o2)
            both["horizon"] = _weeks(both, task)
            frames.append(score_forecasts(both, truth, keys=_KEYS))
            energy.append(energy_scores(both, truth, unit=_KEYS[1:4]))
        # The final-count samples on the latest release's complete weeks.
        final = pd.concat(
            [
                samples.assign(
                    model=key,
                    origin=vintage,
                    target="complete",
                    truth_vintage=latest,
                )
                for key, samples in forecasts.items()
            ],
            ignore_index=True,
        )
        truth = _zone_truth(latest_counts, final, latest).merge(done)
        final["horizon"] = _weeks(final, task)
        frames.append(score_forecasts(final, truth, keys=_KEYS))
        energy.append(energy_scores(final, truth, unit=_KEYS[1:4]))
    if not frames:
        # No origin forecast, as in a block of origins every model skips.
        return pd.DataFrame(), pd.DataFrame(), pd.DataFrame()
    return (
        pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True),
        pd.concat(energy, ignore_index=True),
        pd.concat(kept, ignore_index=True)[
            [
                "model",
                "origin",
                "reference_date",
                "location",
                "target_end_date",
                "sample",
                "value",
            ]
        ],
    )

docs.title: How it is used in the workflow
docs.text: bdbvhub reads the hub's data through this package. uv run bdbvhub data downloads and tidies the hub's streams into data/, and the fit store, the backtest and the submission load them from there. The backtest's tasks come from nowcastbdbv.backtest with the settings in config/backtest.toml. The Fit store workflow (fit-store.yml) refits when the package's data code or that config changes. The workflow's round reports load the target with load_target, and its scoring and ablation rules read the same backtest config. The paper's Ebola study uses the same release backtest.
